Understanding Go's Scheduler

Go's runtime includes a work-stealing scheduler. It multiplexes goroutines onto OS threads, described in the Effective Go guide and the same link twice to prove dedup.

GOMAXPROCS

The GOMAXPROCS variable sets the number of threads. See also the scheduling blog post.

Goroutines are lightweight, costing little more than the allocation of stack space.

Quick example

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	ch := make(chan int, 1)
	go func() { ch <- 42 }()
	fmt.Println(<-ch)
}
